questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A student preparing a sweet drink at home stirs sugar into a glass of water and finds that the first sip taken from the top of the glass is just as sweet as the last sip left at the bottom. Consider the following statements. 1. A well-stirred mixture of sugar and water is a homogeneous mixture, that is, a solution. 2. This is so because the mixture has a uniform composition throughout. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: For the class activity a student prepares three mixtures in beakers: one spatula of common salt stirred well into 50 mL of water, one spatula of chalk powder stirred well into 50 mL of water, and a few drops of milk stirred into 50 mL of water. She then passes the light of a laser pointer through each beaker and watches the beam from the side of the beaker, in a direction perpendicular to the laser beam. Consider the following statements. 1. All three mixtures belong to one and the same type, each of them being a solution that stays homogeneous. 2. This is so because in every beaker the added solid or the milk has dissolved completely, so each of the mixtures has a uniform composition throughout. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A student stirs sand into water in a beaker, leaves the beaker undisturbed on a table, and later finds the sand lying settled at the bottom with clear water standing over it. Consider the following statements. 1. A stirred mixture of sand and water is a heterogeneous mixture. 2. This is so because the sand dissolves in the water, and so the mixture keeps a uniform composition throughout. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
